one_sentence_story: Joseph LeDoux discovered that sensory signals split at the thalamus into TWO speeds: a fast, blurry 'Low Road' straight to the amygdala that makes you jump at a crooked stick in milliseconds, and a slower, sharp 'High Road' through visual cortex that says 'Relax, it's just wood' a split-second later.
so_what_for_you: Forgive your body's first half-second flinch — the Low Road was built to save your life with blurry false alarms; just wait one calm breath for your cortical High Road to inspect whether it's actually a stick.

jargon_map.analogy: like airbags deploying automatically vs the driver feeling shaken afterward
